evidenceProvenance.controller: Windows USB/HID enumeration and Razer Synapse; capture wrapper at 4f2bf1565c7557439760db7e45104bb1e8b62bfd

action.name: Attended USB-only reconnect with 12 V retained
action.value: Operator disconnected USB for about five seconds and reconnected the same port, with HyperBoost inactive and preferred Auto/full-brightness/static-green baseline saved

validation.applyResult: The operator confirmed inactive pad-dependent HyperBoost and normal Auto/static-green baseline before capture. No OpenBlade pad-control report was sent.
validation.readbackResult: Actual USB enumeration binds the pad identity to a successful MI_00 report-descriptor exchange, distinct from injected configuration descriptor data.
validation.restorationResult: Operator answered done, nothing abnormal to the USB-only reconnect and preferred Auto/full-brightness/static-green restoration prompt.
validation.restorationReadbackResult: Vendor startup Auto/brightness traffic was captured. Capture stopped gracefully, without errors, and OpenBlade restarted.

sanitizedEvidence.summary: Post-reconnect device descriptor frame226 identifies VID1532/PID0F43/revision0200. The following actual report-descriptor exchange shares the same USB device and interface zero. Raw root traffic and unrelated descriptors remain private.

The HID GET_DESCRIPTOR_FROM_INTERFACE request asks for report descriptor type22 on interface zero with an 86-byte maximum. Its correlated successful response returns exactly22bytes, the complete descriptor. This is an actual response rather than an injected descriptor-length advertisement.

The full descriptor declares Consumer/ConsumerControl application collection, vendor usageFF00:02, one constant/array/absolute Feature item with ReportSize8 and ReportCount90, then EndCollection. It has no ReportID item. Thus it declares an unnumbered90-byte feature body. Windows HID APIs require prefix zero for an unnumbered report and the independently inventoried FeatureReportByteLength is91. This establishes the buffer choice, not successful OpenBlade feature I/O.

Post-descriptor startup contains a00/84 query returning0000, acknowledged00/04:0300, then00/84 returning0300. Two acknowledged Auto000600 pairs and two full-brightness query/set pairs occur. These are vendor observations with no independent fan or ownership readback.

limitations: AllDevices was used only for bounded descriptor discovery because enumeration and reconnect can change addresses. Unrelated root traffic, serial-bearing startup replies, local paths and instance identifiers are excluded from this annotation.
Descriptor-declared zero prefix and91-byte Windows capability geometry do not establish actual user-mode I/O success, safe OpenBlade handback or autonomous firmware ownership.

The prior in-memory parser returned REPORT_DOES_NOT_EXIST for both candidates. The actual constant Feature descriptor resolves buffer geometry despite that parser result; no fallback-ID experiment was performed.
Raw mode-family values are accessory candidates. Laptop Driver/Normal semantics and fan/RPM interpretation remain unassigned.

productionAdmission.reason: Actual descriptor and Windows metadata establish prefix zero and91-byte buffer for a bounded future query; accessory mutation and actual feature-I/O validation remain closed.

notes: Microsoft HidD_GetFeature/HidD_SetFeature documentation requires a zero first byte when a collection does not include report IDs and uses FeatureReportByteLength as the buffer length.
No vendor process was killed, vendor service stopped, device reset issued or driver restarted. The operator performed the USB-only reconnect.
